problem_text:
A logistics manager must select cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:

* Container 1: volume 37 m³, revenue $53
* Container 2: volume 44 m³, revenue $197
* Container 3: volume 42 m³, revenue $60
* Container 4: volume 7 m³, revenue $263
* Container 5: volume 16 m³, revenue $276
* Container 6: volume 3 m³, revenue $25
* Container 7: volume 46 m³, revenue $54
* Container 8: volume 30 m³, revenue $143
* Container 9: volume 48 m³, revenue $141
* Container 10: volume 45 m³, revenue $297
* Container 11: volume 25 m³, revenue $93
* Container 12: volume 16 m³, revenue $72
* Container 13: volume 44 m³, revenue $275
* Container 14: volume 11 m³, revenue $264
* Container 15: volume 42 m³, revenue $134
* Container 16: volume 1 m³, revenue $125
* Container 17: volume 10 m³, revenue $83
* Container 18: volume 41 m³, revenue $89
* Container 19: volume 49 m³, revenue $100

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 389 m³. Choose the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
